verses.text: Naomi had a relative on her husband's side named Boaz. He was a rich and important man from the clan of Elimelek.
Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields and pick up the leftover grain behind anyone who is kind to me." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter."
So she went out and began picking up grain in the fields behind the harvest workers. As it happened, she ended up working in a field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelek.
Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvest workers, "The LORD be with you!" "The LORD bless you!" they answered.
Boaz asked the man in charge of his workers, "Who does that young woman belong to?"
The man answered, "She is the Moabite woman who came back from Moab with Naomi.

She said, 'Please let me pick up the leftover grain from among the bundles behind the workers.' She came into the field and has kept working from morning till now, except for a short rest in the shelter."
So Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Do not go and pick up grain in another field. Do not go away from here. Stay here with the women who work for me.
Watch where the men are harvesting, and follow along behind the women. I have told the men not to touch you. And whenever you are thirsty, go and get a drink from the water jars the men have filled."
At this, she bowed down with her face to the ground. She asked him, "Why have you been so kind to notice me, a foreigner?"

Boaz replied, "I have been told all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband died. I know how you left your father and mother and your homeland and came to live with a people you did not know before.
May the LORD repay you for what you have done. May you be richly rewarded by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to find shelter."
"May I keep finding favour with you, my lord," she said. "You have comforted me and spoken kindly to me, your servant, even though I am not even one of your servants."

At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce." When she sat down with the harvest workers, he gave her some roasted grain. She ate all she wanted and had some left over.
When she got up to pick up grain again, Boaz told his men, "Let her pick up grain even among the bundles, and do not embarrass her.
Even pull out some stalks for her from the bundles and leave them for her to pick up. Do not tell her off."
So Ruth picked up grain in the field until evening. Then she beat out the barley she had gathered, and it came to about fifteen kilograms.
She carried it back to town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gathered. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had left over after she had eaten enough.

Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you pick up grain today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who noticed you!" Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the one at whose place she had been working. "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz," she said.

"The LORD bless him!" Naomi said to her daughter-in-law. "He has not stopped showing his kindness to the living and the dead." She added, "That man is our close relative. He is one of our family protectors, who can redeem us."
Then Ruth the Moabite said, "He even said to me, 'Stay with my workers until they finish harvesting all my grain.'"
Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good for you, my daughter, to go with the women who work for him. In someone else's field you might be harmed."
So Ruth stayed close to the women of Boaz to pick up grain until the barley and wheat harvests were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.
